stages.name: Awareness
stages.buyer: The buyer does not know they have a problem worth solving, or does not know this category exists. They are reading, listening and comparing themselves to peers.
stages.what: Positioning, brand, content and events that make the company findable and worth a second look.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here turn a vague product into a sharp story, pick the audience and the channel, and build the content engine that keeps showing up. They are usually marketers or founders who have done a category launch.

stages.name: Engage
stages.buyer: The buyer has felt the pain and is actively looking. They are responding to outreach, downloading, attending, and are willing to take a first call.
stages.what: Demand generation, ABM, outbound, AI prospecting, lead routing and the intelligence that decides who to go after.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here build pipeline from nothing. They know how to pick targets, run sequences and campaigns, and get a qualified first meeting on the calendar at a cost that works.

stages.name: Qualify
stages.buyer: The buyer is in a real evaluation. They have a shortlist, a rough budget and a timeline, and they are deciding whether this is the right fit and the right time.
stages.what: Discovery, demos, sales motion design, pipeline inspection and forecasting, competitive positioning and the call intelligence that shows what is working.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here install the process that turns meetings into forecastable deals. Discovery frameworks, demo playbooks, stage definitions and the weekly inspection cadence that keeps a pipeline honest.

stages.name: Commit
stages.buyer: The buyer has chosen and is negotiating. Procurement, security, pricing, contract terms and the internal case to their own leadership.
stages.what: Deal execution, pricing and packaging, negotiation, mutual action plans, co-sell with partners and proposal automation.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here close. They structure deals, defend price, navigate buying committees and get signatures on the date that was forecast.

stages.name: Onboard
stages.buyer: The buyer has signed and is nervous. They want to see value fast, know who to call, and prove to their own boss that this was the right decision.
stages.what: Onboarding and implementation design, success plans, time to value and the sales to CS handoff.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here design the first 90 days of a customer. Kickoffs, milestones, implementation playbooks and the handoff that stops customers falling through the gap after the sale.

stages.name: Adopt
stages.buyer: The buyer is using the product and forming an opinion. Usage is rising or stalling, and the renewal is quietly being decided months before it comes up.
stages.what: Health scoring, adoption programs, QBRs and EBRs, voice of customer, churn analysis and renewal process.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here keep customers. They build the health model, run the business review cadence, spot risk early and turn a wobbly account into a renewal.

stages.name: Expand
stages.buyer: The buyer is happy and has more budget, more teams or more use cases. They will buy more if someone shows them why, and they will refer if asked.
stages.what: Expansion motion, upsell and cross-sell playbooks, account management, advocacy and customer marketing.
stages.skilled: Operators strong here grow accounts. They find the whitespace, build the expansion trigger framework, run strategic account plans and turn customers into references.

foundation.name: Lead & plan
foundation.what: Strategy, positioning, org design, planning, board reporting and interim leadership. Work that sets direction for every stage.

foundation.name: Build the team
foundation.what: Hiring, onboarding, coaching, comp, methodology and manager enablement. Work that makes the people in every stage better.

foundation.name: Systems & data
foundation.what: CRM, reporting, routing, tech stack, ops platforms and AI infrastructure. The plumbing every stage runs on.
